I walked every flow except Cmd+O, which did nothing in the Linux preview (the header glyph opened the chooser). I ran at 1280x800, 1000x700 and a 20px root. The preview page adds a 55px synthetic-workspace banner, so the pane is 55px shorter than the real app. Y values below include that offset.

## 1. Design-specificity verdict

Authored. Several decisions would not survive being lifted into another product:

- Collapsed message rows reuse the list's 132px sender column. Sender sits at x=90 and snippet at x=234, identical in the list and the reader.
- The date stays on the 24px right inset.
- "Saved locally · not sent" sits next to a Details row that says "Cc: Not cached", with a title explaining why. That is the honest-state principle shown in the UI.
- The composer is an inset card with a Graphite underline per field. It is not a modal and has no Send.
- The hostile-markup fixtures render literally.

What reads as generic is the composer card on its own. It is a rounded raised box with a boxed textarea, which is what any mail client ships. The product's character lives in the reader, not the composer.

## 2. Nielsen heuristics

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | The status line, pending state and Saving/Cancel are honest. Focus drops to `<body>` when Save is pressed. The loading skeleton does not hold position. |
| 2 | Match to the real world | 3 | Terse, plain wording ("Cc: Not cached", "Show quoted text"). The two identical clock glyphs in the header are ambiguous. |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc closes the composer and returns focus to the message toggle. Esc on the list restores focus to row 1. R then Esc leaves a blank draft behind (documented as deferred). |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 2 | Docked reply composer inner padding is 10px. The docked New Message card is 16px. Details values are ragged. The chooser list is indented 40px. |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | No Send exists. The recipient address is shown beside the display name. Over-limit files and bidi characters are handled. |
| 6 | Recognition over recall | 3 | The header glyphs carry the shortcut in their titles. There is no visible key hint for N/P/O inside the reader. |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 3 | J/K/N/P/O/R/C/Esc all work and Esc chains correctly. About 19 Tab stops come before the first message. The compose body types at 12px but is read at 15px. |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 3 | Very quiet. The status line, caveat, quote preview, Esc hint and Cc/Subject toggle all sit inside the composer card. The undocked card is a 613px slab with 360px of dead space below the footer. |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry for file details, an alert line for save failure, and honest wording. Not exercised, because the fixtures never fail. |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 3 | Detail lives in titles and the caveat toggle; there is no cheat sheet. The palette lists Keys. |

**Total 29/40, Good (lower edge).**

## 3. Cognitive load

Failures: 3 of 8, which is moderate load.

- **Single focus: fail in the docked composer.** With a reply open, the thread is squeezed to a sliver. At 1280x800 the scroller drops to 241px with Cc/Subject open. The message being replied to is hidden behind its own composer (its quote sits inside the card).
- **Minimal choices: fail at the header.** Eleven glyphs (the banner note is not one) plus 5 rail stops come before any message. They include two identical clocks and two "Reply" controls (header and per-message).
- **Grouping: fail in Details.** The values start at x=126, 109, 111 and 124 for From, To, Cc and Sent.

Passing: hierarchy, chunking, one thing at a time, working memory, progressive disclosure. The Cc/Subject toggle, caveat toggle and quote toggle are good progressive disclosure.

Decision points with more than 4 visible options: the reader header (about 12 glyphs) and the compact row of reply controls. In the composer itself there are at most 4 controls per state.

## 4. Emotional journey

- **Peak:** J, N, O and Details all behave predictably. The geometry never shifts between conversations. A participant's focus ring is clear. This feels precise.
- **Valley 1:** pressing Enter or clicking Save on an attachment drops focus to the page. The keyboard user loses their place.
- **Valley 2:** R opens a composer that covers half the pane and pushes the contact pane down 33px.
- **End:** Esc returns focus to the message toggle, so the close is clean. In the preview the status line is amber "Saved in preview memory (non-durable) · not sent". That is honest but anxious for a user who just typed. Real state reads Ash.

## 5. Strengths, priority issues, contradicted claims

**Strengths**

1. **Grid parity.** Subject, sender, body, Details and attachments all sit at x=90, the same x as the list sender text. Collapsed rows hit the same x as the list's snippet column (234). The message fill is 46 to 1002 (6px from the 40 and 1008 pane edges), so opening a row never shifts the text edge. J/K lands the same boxes.
2. **Participant focus and Details.** The 2px lavender outline at 1px offset is plainly visible on keyboard focus (verified). The Details glyph is generated content with an empty alt. Cc says "Not cached", never "none".
3. **Safe, honest rendering.** `<script>` and `<img onerror>` render as literal text everywhere. Names are never trusted as markup.

**Priority issues**

- **P1 — Save drops focus to `<body>`.**
  - **What:** In `MessageAttachments.vue`, the Save button is swapped for Saving…/Cancel. Pressing Enter on Save moved `document.activeElement` to BODY (verified). The Retry path has a focus watcher; Save does not.
  - **Why it matters:** Keyboard-first and screen-reader users lose their place on every download.
  - **Fix:** Keep one button mounted (the Retry pattern, `aria-disabled`, label swap), or move focus to the row group and back.
  - **Command:** `/impeccable harden`
- **P1 — Skeleton jumps by 56px, contradicting the claim.**
  - **What:** The row pitch is right (49px each, matching 40.99px + 8px). But in the identity-known case the first skeleton row starts at y=244.3 while the first real message starts at 187.9. The "Loading conversation…" line and the sender/date line push everything down 56px.
  - **Why it matters:** The pane jumps on every J.
  - **Fix:** Fold the status line into the identity line, or reserve its height with the same margins as the loaded meta row.
  - **Command:** `/impeccable polish`
- **P2 — Contact pane shifts while composing a reply.**
  - **What:** "Composing to Ada Fixture / ada@example.test" is inserted at the top (y=55 to 87). The contact name moves from y=87 to 120 and the email from 143 to 176. The new text sits in the header band.
  - **Why it matters:** It breaks the "name on the tab line, email on the first-row line" rule and moves things at the moment you start typing.
  - **Fix:** Keep the pinned lines fixed and put "Composing to…" below the thread list, or drop it.
  - **Command:** `/impeccable layout`
- **P2 — Ragged Details columns.**
  - **What:** `.message-field-label` has no fixed width, so the values start at four different x positions.
  - **Fix:** Give the label column a fixed width (about 3rem) or use a grid.
  - **Command:** `/impeccable polish`
- **P2 — Composer geometry is inconsistent.**
  - **What:** The undocked card is 613px tall (139 to 752) with the footer at y=382 and the rest empty. The reply composer's inner padding is 10px (content at x=101) while the docked new-message card is 16px (x=107). The chooser file list is indented 40px (x=328 against 288 for the text above it).
  - **Fix:** Pin the footer to the bottom or size the card to its content, share one padding value, and zero the chooser list padding.
  - **Command:** `/impeccable layout`
- **P3 — Identical clock glyphs.**
  - **What:** "Remind me on this device" (x=688) and "Reminders" (x=880) are the same clock SVG. Reply also appears twice.
  - **Fix:** A bell or a different mark for the per-conversation reminder.
  - **Command:** `/impeccable clarify`

**Claims in DESIGN.md that the render contradicts**

- **Skeleton:** "so the pane does not jump when the conversation arrives." Measured 244.3 against 187.9 (a 56px offset). The 49px pitch itself is verified.
- **"One x" for Details:** "The collapsed sender, the expanded body, the signature and `Details` share one x." True for Details (90), but the Details values are at 126, 109, 111 and 124.
- **Contact pane alignment:** the email sits at 143 while composing a reply in the contact pane, not on the "first list line" (96px from content top).

**Claims confirmed, with numbers**

- **50px inset:** subject, sender, body and Details all at x=90. List sender at 90. Date right edge 984 (24px from 1008).
- **Message fill:** 46 to 1002. Active message: Lifted Charcoal `rgb(51,49,46)` plus a 3px lavender inset bar.
- **Composer margins:** `6px 24px 12px 50px`, box 90 to 984, both docked and undocked (docked radius 6px, undocked 10px).
- **Caveat target:** 24×24px with 5px padding and −3px margin (glyph 14×14).
- **Field underline:** Graphite `rgb(142,138,135)`, 3.79:1 on the card. Seam is 1.36:1. The textarea border is the same Graphite on all four sides. I computed these from the live colours, not from a pixel sample.
- **Reading body:** 15px, 24px line height, max 620px (65ch). Subject 16px at weight 600. Mono block 13.6px at 720px.
- **20px root:** the reader scales, with rows at 51px. The composer is capped at 59% of the pane, so only 225px of thread remains.

## 6. Persona red flags

- **Alex (power user):** The compose body types at 12px while the reading body is 15px. After R, the thread is mostly covered (the scroller is 225px at a 20px root). There is no key to jump from a quoted message to its own Reply. About 19 Tab stops precede the first message, though J/K/N/P/O make that moot.
- **Sam (accessibility/keyboard):** Save drops focus to BODY. The active-message bar is both the "active" and the "focus" indicator on the message toggle, so you cannot tell where focus is. Header glyphs come first in DOM order, ahead of any message, with no skip link. At a 20px root the reply glyph's box stays 24px around a 20px icon. Two controls are both named "Reply". Positives: participants announce "Name, mailbox", the Details marker has an empty alt, and the status line is not a live region.
- **Riley (stress tester):** R then Esc leaves a blank local draft (documented as deferred). The New Message card shows the stale focused conversation's contact. The Save status line persists in the message after the chooser closes. Hostile names and subjects render safely and wrap in the contact pane.
- **Triager (project persona, the single-author dogfooder):**
  - **Profile:** Processes 100+ threads a session, mostly Reply-then-move-on.
  - **Behaviors:** Skims the Reply preview, rarely uses Details, trusts the status line.
  - **Red flags:** The composer hides the message being answered. The status line reads amber and anxious in the preview. No Send, so the triager must always leave for the provider client. A save failure on an attachment has no visible cue to the keyboard.

## 7. Minor observations and provocative questions

**Minor**

- Hairlines between collapsed messages at 46 to 1002 look like list dividers; the Seams-Only Rule is bent for the reader.
- The Show quoted text ghost button text sits at x=98, 8px inside the 90 text edge. The Save text in the attachment row does the same.
- The Esc hint is bare text beside Save and close. It reads as a label, not a key.
- The synthetic fixtures have no read-state line, so that line was never rendered.
- The reader header shows `— you@fixture.emailos` (account address) in every reader state.
- Signature and quote share one 15px Ash style, so they are not distinguishable from each other.

**Questions**

1. If the thread is the reason to reply, why does the composer get to cover it? Should the composer scroll the latest message into a fixed, visible strip?
2. The product's promise is honest state. Why is the least honest state, a Save that silently moves focus, the one the keyboard user hits most?
3. Is the composer card a decision about design (an inset card with a field underline), or a default that happened to line up with the inset?

content.text:
Method: dual-agent (A: design review driving the real render · B: detector and in-page overlay). Both ran in isolated sub-agents. Together they gave the first rendered look at this area, since the earlier pass was source-only. Nothing was edited. The assessments used the fixture preview in the T3 browser at 1280×800, 1000×700 and a 20px root font.

## Design Health Score: 29/40, Good (lower edge)

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | Honest status line and pending state. **Save drops focus to `<body>`**, and the loading skeleton does not hold position. |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 3 | Terse, plain wording (`Cc: Not cached`, `Show quoted text`). Two identical clock glyphs in the header. |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc chains correctly and returns focus. R then Esc leaves a blank draft (deferred by design). |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 2 | Docked reply padding is 10px, the docked new-message card 16px. Details values start at four different x's. The chooser list is indented 40px. |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | No Send. Address shown beside the display name. |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 3 | Shortcuts are in the glyph titles. No visible N/P/O hint in the reader. |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 3 | J/K/N/P/O/R/C/Esc all work. Compose body types at 12px but is read at 15px. |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 3 | Very quiet. The undocked card is a 613px slab with about 360px of dead space under the footer. |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry, alert lines, honest wording. Failure paths were not exercised (fixtures never fail). |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 3 | Detail lives in titles and the caveat toggle. No cheat sheet. |
| **Total** | | **29/40** | Good |

Trend, noting that the scores come from three different assessors: 23 (first pass, source only) → 28 (input to this task, source only) → 29 (now, rendered).

## Design specificity verdict

**Design review:** the area feels authored for this product. Collapsed message rows reuse the list's 132px sender column, so the sender lands at x=90 and the snippet at x=234 in both list and reader. Honest state shows up as `Saved locally · not sent` next to `Cc: Not cached`. The composer is an inset card with no Send. The one generic part is the composer card on its own: a rounded raised box with a boxed textarea, which any mail client ships. The product's character lives in the reader, not the composer.

**Deterministic scan:**
- The six reader/compose `.vue` files, `App.vue`, and the layout and type scopes all return 0 findings, the same as baseline.
- `style.css` has 6 findings, all pre-existing and none on a reader or composer selector.
  - 3 side-tab hits are the documented focus bar, so likely false positives.
  - 3 radius advisories (2px, 2px, 3px) are real but outside this area.
- The change set removed 3 earlier `rgba(0,0,0,0.35)` colour advisories.

**Overlay:**
- The in-page detector ran in three states: reader with Details open, reply composer, and new-message card.
- Reader and reply were clean.
- The new-message card raised `flat-type-hierarchy` (body 12px, h2 12px, h3 12px). That rule is identical at the pre-change baseline. DESIGN.md says weight, not size, separates levels in the shell, so I treat it as a false positive.
- The `[Human]` overlay was not shown to you, because the preview tab was closed.

## Overall impression

The inset work landed. For the first time this was measured, and the grid holds. The remaining defects are all behavioural or rhythmic, which source reading and jsdom could not catch. The biggest opportunity is the reply composer: it covers the thread it answers.

## What's working

1. **Grid parity.**
   - Subject, sender, body, Details and attachments all sit at x=90, the same x as the list sender text.
   - The message fill is 46 to 1002, which is 6px inside the pane edges.
   - The date's right edge is 24px in.
   - Docked and undocked composers share the same box (90 to 984).
   - Opening a row does not shift the text edge.
2. **Participants and Details.** The 2px lavender focus ring is clearly visible. The participant name reads "Name, mailbox". The Details marker is announced with an empty alt.
3. **Safe, honest rendering.** Hostile markup renders literally everywhere. Cc says "Not cached", never "none". The status line is not a live region.

Claims confirmed by measurement:
- Caveat toggle is 24×24.
- Field underline and textarea border are Graphite, 3.79:1 against the card, versus Seam at 1.36:1.
- Reading body is 15px/24px at a 620px max width.
- Every interactive control shows the 2px ring except the active message toggle, which is deliberate.
- The only live region in the composer is the one hidden status span.

## Priority issues

**[P1] Saving an attachment drops focus to `<body>`**
- *Why it matters:* a keyboard or screen-reader user loses their place on every download.
- *Fix:* `MessageAttachments` swaps the Save button for `Saving…` and `Cancel`. Keep one button mounted, using the same pattern Retry now uses, or move focus into the row and back.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable harden`

**[P1] The loading skeleton still jumps, contradicting the DESIGN.md claim**
- *Measured:* the 49px row pitch is correct. But with a known identity, the first skeleton row starts at y=244.3 while the first real message starts at y=187.9, a 56px offset. The `Loading conversation…` line and the sender/date line push everything down. The fixture loads instantly, so A measured a replica built from the same markup and CSS, not a real load.
- *Why it matters:* the pane jumps on every J.
- *Fix:* fold the status line into the identity line, or reserve its height with the loaded meta row's margins.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable polish`

**[P2] The contact pane shifts while a reply is open**
- *What:* `Composing to Ada Fixture / ada@example.test` is inserted at the top. The contact name moves from y=87 to 120 and the email from 143 to 176. This is an existing behaviour that run 1 recorded as "seen but out of scope", not caused by this change set.
- *Why it matters:* it breaks DESIGN.md's rule that the name sits on the tab line and the email on the first-list line, at the moment you start typing.
- *Fix:* drop the line, or move it below the thread list.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable layout`

**[P2] Details columns are ragged, so "one x" is only half true**
- *What:* Details sits at x=90, but its values start at 126, 109, 111 and 124 for From, To, Cc and Sent. `.message-field-label` has no fixed width.
- *Fix:* give the label a fixed width (about 3rem) or use a two-column grid.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable polish`

**[P2] Composer geometry is inconsistent and covers the thread**
- *What:*
  - The reply composer's inner padding is 10px; the docked new-message card's is 16px.
  - The undocked new-message card is 613px tall with the footer at y=382.
  - The chooser file list is indented 40px against its text above.
  - With Cc/Subject open the thread scroller drops to 241px at 1280×800. At a 20px root only 225px of thread remains, and the message being answered sits behind its own composer.
- *Fix:* one shared padding, a card sized to its content, a zero-indent chooser list, and keep the replied-to message visible above the card.
- *Suggested command:* `/impeccable layout`

## Persona red flags

- **Alex (power user):** the compose body types at 12px but reads at 15px. After R the thread is mostly covered. The reader has about 19 Tab stops before the first message (A counted the header glyphs and rail). B counted 5 inside the reader with Details open and 11 with the reply composer, so the two counts differ in scope.
- **Sam (accessibility/keyboard):** Save drops focus. The active-message bar is both the "active" and the "focus" indicator on the toggle, so you cannot tell where focus is. Header glyphs precede any message with no skip link. Two controls are both named "Reply". Positives: participants announce correctly, and the Details marker has an empty alt.
- **Riley (stress tester):** R then Esc leaves a blank draft (deferred by design). The New Message card shows the stale focused conversation's contact. The Save status line persists after the chooser closes. Two under-24px targets in the open reader: the `Details` summary (16px high) and the participant spans (16px high).
- **The single-author triager (project persona):** the composer hides the message being answered. The preview's amber `non-durable` status reads anxious right after typing. There is no Send, so every finished reply means leaving for the provider client, which is the stated design.

## Minor observations

- The hairlines between collapsed messages (46 to 1002) look like list dividers and bend the Seams-Only Rule.
- The `Show quoted text` and `Save` ghost buttons place their text 8px inside the 90px text edge.
- The Esc hint is bare text beside `Save and close`, so it reads as a label rather than a key.
- Signature and quote share one 15px Ash style, so they cannot be told apart.
- B measured 1–3px horizontal overflow on `.message-toggle`, `.composer-top` and `.composer-status-group`, and 20px-root ellipsis clipping on the contact-pane buttons. All of it is clipped text or sub-4px; none reaches the page level.
- The reader's read-state line, quote, signature, multi-recipient and attachment-failure states are absent from the fixtures, so they were never rendered.

## Claims in DESIGN.md that the render contradicts

- **Skeleton:** "so the pane does not jump when the conversation arrives." Measured as a 56px offset on a replica.
- **"One x":** "the collapsed sender, the expanded body, the signature and `Details` share one x." The label sits at x=90, but the values do not.
- **Contact pane alignment:** the email is at 143, not on the first-list line, while a reply is open.

Not verified: Cmd+O on Linux (the header glyph path worked), the real Gmail-state wording, a true loading state, quote/mono split on real messages, screen-reader announcements, and pixel-sampled contrast.
